text.content:
This part follows a rigger and their machines: taking a drone out of the sheet, controlling it by hand, remotely or jumped in, sharing autosofts from the console, then transforming the drone at the Workshop, buying a new one at the dealership, launching it in a chase, forming a swarm and jamming the drones opposite. The player who plays a rigger reads the whole part; the GM mostly reads chapters 6.2 (what they install without a test), 6.4 (they are the one who runs the chase) and the settings tables.

The system applies the core rulebook's rigging rules (Core Rulebook p. 264-270) and its chases (Core Rulebook p. 198-204); when the GM ticks them, those of Rigger 5.0. This manual does not copy them: it shows the windows, says what the system computes on its own and what stays in the GM's hands.

All

What it is for

A drone or vehicle owned by a character first lives as an item on their sheet. Once deployed, it becomes a separate actor, with its own sheet and token, which is driven in three ways: by hand, remotely through a commlink or a console, or jumped in, the rigger "inside" the machine. This chapter shows these gestures, what jumping in changes to the rolls, what happens to the rigger when their drone is hit or destroyed, and how the rigger command console shares its autosofts with the drones.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU}

pages.name: Deploying a drone, reading its sheet

text.content:
Step by step: deploying and recalling

  1. Open the rigger's sheet, Gear tab, Vehicles & Drones block: each drone and each vehicle has its line.

  2. Click the line's deploy icon (①, Deploy Drone/Vehicle). The system creates the drone's actor, with the rigger as controller; it appears in the Actors tab. Drag it onto the scene to place its token.

  3. A deployed line carries the reversed icon (②). Click it to recall the drone: its damage, modifications, gear and description go back to the sheet's item, and will leave with it at the next deployment.

A deployed drone takes the black-background actor icon of other drone tokens. A drone deployed with an old alpha keeps its picture: recall it then redeploy it. When the GM hides a drone's token, its owner keeps the drone's icon in their PAN crown; the others do not see it.

The drone's sheet

The sheet of a deployed drone or vehicle has its vehicle attributes (Handling, Speed, Acceleration, Body, Armor, Pilot, Sensor, Seats), its resistances, and at the bottom its condition monitor and its Matrix monitor.

  • ① Vehicle Actions: Vehicle Test, Ram, Autopilot facing the unexpected (on autopilot), Active targeting and Repair, each with its pool and limit: a click on the figure rolls the test.

  • ② The Control mode block says who drives and how; its lines are detailed below.

  • The mode (the list under Controller): Autopilot, Remote (through a commlink or a console), Manual (someone on board, at the controls) and Rigging (jumped in).

  • The Controller: the character who drives. It is their skill, control rig, console and Edge that the system reads. The icon at the top of the block lets you choose another one.

  • Slaved Device: the drone is a slave of the controller's master device (commlink, cyberdeck or console). It defends in the Matrix with that master's Firewall, it is drawn under it in the PAN crown (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.CKM0UvZC23LLnCgv.JournalEntryPage.4tswtGQqbgDVe9IS]{the PAN crown}), and it receives the autosofts shared by a console. Under the box: Direct connection to the rigger (@UUID[.EeofjxxUXrEEcUdb]{noise}) and Swarm no. (@UUID[.OfCIohrhdBY7Vzxg]{swarms}). It is a single gesture: adding the vehicle to the PAN from the rigger's sheet ticks this box, and ticking it on the drone puts it in the master's PAN list (if there is room left). Removing the vehicle from the list or unticking the box undoes both.

  • The Current Speed: the speed at which the drone is moving right now, 0 when stopped. The chase reads and writes it, as do two Rigger 5.0 qualities, Speed Demon and Information Overload (Rigger 5.0 p. 33-34).

The sheet's tabs, at the top, also give the drone's modifications and gear, its Workshop (the gears icon, @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2}) and its description. Every drone has the rigger interface by default (Core Rulebook p. 269): the Rigger Interface box is ticked and greyed. For a vehicle, it must be ticked for jumping in to be offered.

pages.name: Taking control: manual, remote, jumped in

text.content:
Choose the mode in the drone sheet's Control mode block, and the driver as Controler. Rolls are made from the drone's sheet; the system takes the pool and limit that suit the mode, and shows them in the Vehicule Actions block.

ModeWho rollsWhat the system changes
Autopilotthe drone itself: Pilot + autosoftthe autosofts installed on the drone, or shared by the console; never Edge
Manualthe driver on board: driving skill + Reaction [Handling]penalty for an ork, an elf, a dwarf or a troll at the controls of an unadapted vehicle (Rigger 5.0 p. 169)
Remotethe controller, through their commlink or console (Core Rulebook p. 237)each limit capped by the Data Processing of the commanding device; +2 to the limit of a driver in VR (Core Rulebook p. 201); the noise of distance
Rigging (jumped in)the rigger, through their control riglimits + 2 (VR) + control rig rating; pool of vehicle tests + control rig rating; threshold of vehicle tests − rating, never below 1; +1 die in hot sim (Core Rulebook p. 201, 266)

Step by step: jumping into a drone

  1. Check that the rigger has a Control Rig (an implant), or the Machine Mind echo if they are a technomancer (Core Rulebook p. 258). Without one or the other, the Rigging mode is not offered: they drive remotely.

  2. On the drone's sheet, choose the rigger as Controler, then the Rigging mode. The figures of the Vehicle Actions block change at once.

  3. Click the Vehicle Test figure: the roll window details the pool (the rigger's skill, plus their control rig), the limit (base, Virtual Reality, control rig) and the threshold reduction.

Only vehicle skill tests (vehicle test, ramming, Gunnery) receive the control rig's dice; Perception, stealth and the drone's defense only receive the raise of their limit (Core Rulebook p. 266). Jumped in, the drone's stealth is rolled with the rigger's Sneaking + Intuition; remotely, with the Sneaking and Agility of whoever controls. The window offers Push the Limit: the driver's Edge counts on all vehicle tests, by hand, remotely or jumped in, never for the autopilot.

pages.name: VR: cold sim, hot sim, biofeedback, dumpshock

text.content:
Jumping in means being in virtual reality (Core Rulebook p. 266). The rigger's user mode, on their sheet (Matrix tab, under their console: ① of the figure in @UUID[.JH8cbHBFgEXDCGwG]{the console}), says which: Cold-Sim Virtual Reality or Hot-Sim Virtual Reality. Hot sim gives +1 die to all vehicle actions, but makes biofeedback damage Physical.

Jumping in puts you in VR, even if the sheet says AR

A jumped-in rigger is always in VR: if their sheet stayed on Augmented Reality, the system treats them as in cold-sim VR (biofeedback and dumpshock as Stun). Switch their sheet to hot sim if that is what they chose: nothing does it for them.

Biofeedback

A drone hit while its rigger is jumped in sends them half the damage as biofeedback (Core Rulebook p. 266): Stun in cold sim, Physical in hot sim. The Resist Biofeedback Damage window opens for the rigger's player, if they are connected, otherwise for the GM. The drone's tactile sensors cost them 2 dice on this roll (Rigger 5.0 p. 168).

Ejection

The jumped-in rigger is ejected when their drone is destroyed (full condition monitor) or bricked (full Matrix monitor), or when the console or commlink they use is bricked (Core Rulebook p. 266, 269). They suffer dumpshock (Core Rulebook p. 228): the Resist to Dumpshock window opens for their player. The drone switches to Autopilot, out of control until the start of the next turn, then the autopilot takes over; a destroyed or bricked drone does not take over, and the message says so. A rigger who was driving remotely is not ejected.

A drone destroyed by an attack during the jump gives two resistances: biofeedback and dumpshock. They arrive one after the other: the second window opens once the first has been rolled (or closed).

pages.name: The console: noise reduction, sharing, autosofts

text.content:
The rigger command console (RCC) is a Matrix device with two ratings of its own, Noise Reduction and Sharing, whose total never exceeds the Device Rating (Core Rulebook p. 266).

Step by step: setting up the console and sharing autosofts

  1. On the rigger's sheet, open the left Matrix tab: the equipped console shows its Device Rating, the user mode (①) and, under Matrix Attributes, Noise Reduction and Sharing (②). A right-click raises a rating, a left-click lowers it.

  2. In the right Matrix tab, Programs list, each autosoft carries a sharing icon (③, Share with the drones). Click it for the autosofts the console must share, as many as the Sharing rating: beyond, the system refuses and says so. Load them too (Running column).

  3. On the sheet of each drone that should benefit, tick Slaved Device and leave it on Autopilot.

A drone receives the shared and active autosofts if it is on autopilot, slaved, and if its controller has the console equipped (Core Rulebook p. 266). A drone running its own autosofts receives none from the console. On its sheet, each console autosoft is marked: used, shared but set aside, or not shared; hover over the icon to know why. An autosoft installed on the drone runs at most at its Pilot rating (Rigger 5.0 p. 127).

In combat, loading an autosoft (on the console or on the drone) costs a Complex Action; unloading it is free.

← @UUID[.c2kfVj88S2XB0ijl]{VR: cold sim, hot sim, biofeedback, dumpshock} · @UUID[.EeofjxxUXrEEcUdb]{Noise between the rigger and their drones} →

pages.name: Noise between the rigger and their drones

text.content:
A drone driven remotely or jumped in suffers the noise of the distance that separates it from its rigger (Core Rulebook p. 230, 266). The system measures this distance between the two tokens, on the displayed scene, and adds the Noise (distance to the rigger) line in the roll window of each of the drone's actions (vehicle test, ramming, shooting, skill, sensor targeting), minus the console's noise reduction. Neither defenses nor resistances receive it, nor a drone on autopilot or driven on board.

  • Direct connection to the rigger (the drone's Control mode block): the drone is linked by a cable, no noise.

  • A relay unit installed on another drone of the same rigger acts as a relay: the system takes the best path and counts the worst of its legs (Rigger 5.0 p. 168).

  • If one of the two tokens is not on the displayed scene, nothing is counted: the GM adds the noise by hand, like that of a jammed area.

pages.name: What the system does and references

text.content:
What the system does on its own

  • It computes the pool, limit and threshold of each vehicle roll according to the control mode, the control rig and VR.

  • It shares the ticked autosofts with slaved drones on autopilot, within the Sharing limit.

  • It opens biofeedback and dumpshock resistance for the rigger's player, switches the drone to autopilot and hands control back to the autopilot the next turn.

  • It measures the noise between the rigger and each of their drones, relays included.

What the GM does by hand

  • Rolls dumpshock when the cable of a direct connection is torn out: the system does not know this case.

  • Adds the noise of a jammed area, or of two tokens that are not on the same scene.

  • Judges what follows an autopilot facing the unexpected: the line of the same name rolls Device Rating × 2 against the threshold they set.

References

  • Driving in AR or VR: (Core Rulebook p. 201). Rigging, control rig, jumping in, biofeedback: (Core Rulebook p. 264-266). Rigger command console: (Core Rulebook p. 266-268). Drones: (Core Rulebook p. 269-270). Noise: (Core Rulebook p. 230). Dumpshock: (Core Rulebook p. 229). Autosoft cap: (Rigger 5.0 p. 127).

  • The exhaustive detail: wiki: Rigging.

All

What it is for

The Workshop is the tab where you transform a drone or a vehicle: buying a modification, installing it by the book (the mechanic's extended test), removing it, or, for the GM, fitting it with a click. It counts the slots of each category, or a drone's Modification Points if the table plays that rule, and refuses what does not fit. Damage is also repaired there.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU}

← @UUID[.7KsLUCEMib3roEF5]{What the system does and references} · @UUID[.046XTGe9sFUnz4An]{The Workshop tab} →

Open the sheet of a deployed drone, or that of the vehicle item on its owner's sheet, and click the gears icon.

  • ① The gauges: around the vehicle's image (failing that, its category's image), the six categories (Power Train, Protection, Weapons, Body, Electromagnetic, Cosmetic), each with as many slots as the Body (Rigger 5.0 p. 151-152). A full gauge is coloured. Under Modification Points, a single gauge replaces them (@UUID[.rMDDQRPY8b6JXf09]{below}).

  • ② The cost: bare vehicle + modifications = total, and who pays, with their balance. Factory equipment counts 0: it is paid for with the vehicle, and it takes no slot (Rigger 5.0 p. 189).

  • ③ The dice: Install by the book (extended test) on a modification aboard, to be installed; on an installed modification, remove it by the book.

  • ④ The key: Fit directly (GM), or take it off, without test or payment.

Each line gives the slots (or MP), the threshold, the tools and the price of the modification on this vehicle: some prices are multiplied by Handling, Speed or the vehicle's price (Rigger 5.0 p. 155).

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2 The Workshop}

← @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2 The Workshop} · @UUID[.uoPEUL919825Gedn]{Buying, installing, removing} →

Step by step: buying a modification

  1. Open a compendium of vehicle modifications (the Mégapack's), and drag the modification onto the deployed drone's Workshop.

  2. A window gives its category, its slots (or MP), its threshold and tools, its price on this vehicle and who pays. Click Buy: the purchase goes through the shop, with its usual checks (authorized buyer, balance, creation, availability), and the rigger is debited (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.zKky8MvmSeq77inw]{the shop}).

  3. The modification arrives aboard, to be installed: its line says so, greyed. A modification dragged from a character's inventory comes aboard without payment (Put aboard, to be installed).

Step by step: installing by the book

  1. On the line of a modification to install, click the dice icon.

  2. The Install a mod window offers the Mechanic (the selected token, otherwise your character, otherwise the vehicle's owner), their Mechanic Skill depending on the vehicle (editable) and the Mechanic's tools. Confirm.

  3. The roll window opens: it is an extended Mechanic + Logic [Logic] test, the modification's threshold, interval 1 hour (Rigger 5.0 p. 151); tools below those required cost −2 dice, no tools −4 dice, already set; plans and working conditions are added there.

  4. Once the threshold is reached, the card offers Install: a click fits the modification, and its effects apply to the sheet.

  • No room: a modification that does not fit (slots or MP) is refused before the test, with the count in the message ("3 slot(s) needed… 1 left"). The GM can lift this refusal with the Objects rule lock (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.yj32FTBiKvVIyGIf]{the locks}).

  • Critical glitch: the parts are lost; the card's button removes the modification from the vehicle, without refund.

  • Special skill: a modification that requires one recalls it; that test is rolled by hand from the sheet.

  • Removing: the dice icon of an installed modification rolls the same test at the threshold divided by two, rounded up. The book does not give a figure for removal (Rigger 5.0 p. 152): the system makes that choice. The removed modification stays aboard, to be installed.

The GM's direct fit

The GM drags a modification and chooses Fit directly (GM), or clicks a line's key: no test, no payment. On the vehicle item (not deployed), only the GM fits or takes off; buying and installing are done on the deployed drone. The refusal for lack of room applies to them too.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2 The Workshop}

← @UUID[.046XTGe9sFUnz4An]{The Workshop tab} · @UUID[.rMDDQRPY8b6JXf09]{Drone Modification Points} →

The Drone modifications setting offers the optional Rigger 5.0 rule: Modification Points (MP) instead of slots (Rigger 5.0 p. 122-124). It only targets drones: a vehicle always keeps its six categories. A drone's Workshop and dealership then show a single gauge, Modification Points, and the MP column replaces the slots one.

  • The pool: as many MP as the Body. When the book writes Body X(Y), the GM enters Y in the Workshop's Points left (Y): field (the player reads it without changing it); empty, it is the Body.

  • Factory equipment is free and takes no MP (Rigger 5.0 p. 189): a new Steel Lynx keeps its 6 MP for your own modifications, its factory mount included in the profile.

  • Raising an attribute (Handling, Speed, Acceleration, Armor, Sensor): +1 free, once per drone, then the amount minus 1 (+2 Speed costs 1 MP). An attribute never exceeds double its starting value. Armor counts in steps of 3 points, with no cap at double, but beyond 3 × Body it removes Handling, Speed and Acceleration.

  • Weapon mounts follow the book's table according to the weapon's category, from Micro (0) to Heavy (6), +1 for an internal or concealed mount (Rigger 5.0 p. 124). The vehicles' Light mount, absent from the table, costs 3 MP: the book does not give a figure, it is the system's choice.

  • Replacements: Sensor Replacement counts as a Sensor increase up to its rating; Pilot Replacement costs no MP (the book gives it none).

  • Lowering an attribute gives back 1 MP in all. Lowering Body gives back 1 MP per point, but never below half the starting Body, rounded up (Rigger 5.0 p. 123): a Body 3 goes down to 2, not to 1. A drop below is refused, with this floor in the message. The French text writes "rounded down", but its own example reasons with rounding up: the system follows the example.

An installation that exceeds the MP left is refused, for the player as for the GM; a modification that does not ask for more MP is never refused. The window that opens when you drop a modification announces the MP it will take.

An attribute improvement takes the book's Availability (Handling, Speed, Sensor: new value × 2; Acceleration: × 4; Armor: the new value, Restricted beyond 6, Forbidden beyond 12), in the Workshop, at the dealership and at the till (Rigger 5.0 p. 123-124). Below Handling 1, or at Speed or Acceleration 0, the drone's sheet shows This drone can no longer move (Rigger 5.0 p. 124).

Factory equipment on a drone from an old Mégapack version

The system recognizes factory equipment by the modification's Factory box, or by the mark the Mégapack puts on its copies in its recent versions. A drone taken from an older version, or made by hand, can have a factory mount that still counts its MP and its price: open the modification's sheet and tick Factory.

The price follows the book too

Under MP, an attribute increase is paid at the book's price: new value × Body × 200 ¥ (double for Speed; new value × 1,000 ¥ for Sensor) (Rigger 5.0 p. 123). The purchase window announces the modification's cost as if it were alone; the installed line counts the free +1 already taken.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2 The Workshop}

← @UUID[.uoPEUL919825Gedn]{Buying, installing, removing} · @UUID[.s29VMbSZRxv8Nzt4]{Repairing} →

The sheet's Vehicule Actions block has a Repair line (the wrench) (Rigger 5.0 p. 29-30).

Step by step: repairing a drone or a vehicle

  1. Select the mechanic's token, then click the wrench on the vehicle's sheet.

  2. The window announces the damage boxes and the cost of spare parts (5% of the vehicle's price per box). Choose the Method, the Mechanic Skill (depending on the vehicle), the Boxes to repair (threshold) and, if some are missing, the Boxes without spare parts.

  3. Click Repair: it is an extended Mechanic + Logic [Mental] test, interval 4 hours (1 day and −4 dice per box without parts). Once the threshold is reached, the card offers to repair N boxes, which erases them from the monitor.

A vehicle equipped with the nanomaintenance system offers two more methods: autonomous nanomaintenance (the rating in dice, 1 hour) or assisted (the rating added to the mechanic) (Rigger 5.0 p. 166). A vehicle whose boxes are all filled is wrecked: it can no longer be repaired.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.EL4Y6kscI8gvJoJd]{6.2 The Workshop}

← @UUID[.rMDDQRPY8b6JXf09]{Drone Modification Points} · @UUID[.YTo9Tb6Bw8fuLkyp]{What the system does, settings and references} →

pages.name: What the system does, settings and references

text.content:
What the system does on its own

  • It computes the price of each modification on this vehicle, counts slots or MP, and refuses before the test what does not fit.

  • It has the purchase paid through the shop, prepares the test for installing, removing or repairing, and applies the result with a click.

  • It applies the effects of recognized modifications (replacements, Armor cap, tactile sensors, signature masking, metahuman adaptation, passenger protection system…).

What the GM does by hand

  • Enters the Y of a Body X(Y) drone in the Workshop, under MP.

  • Rolls the special skill test of a modification that requires one, and judges the working conditions.

  • Debits the spare parts of a repair, which the system announces without taking them.

Related settings

Setting (Rigging tab of Shadowrun settings)Default
Drone modificationsSlots (main rule); Modification Points (optional) as an option
Objects rule lock (a modification with no room)active: fitting is refused

References

  • Slots and installation: (Rigger 5.0 p. 151-155). Modification Points: (Rigger 5.0 p. 122-124); drone table: (Rigger 5.0 p. 189). Repairing: (Rigger 5.0 p. 29-30); nanomaintenance: (Rigger 5.0 p. 166).

  • wiki: Rigging (Workshop, Modification Points, Repairing).

All

What it is for

The dealership is a window where you build a drone or a vehicle before buying it: you choose the model, add modifications, and see at a glance its gauges, price and availability. The purchase goes through the shop, the whole lot or nothing.

Step by step: building and buying

  1. Click the car-shaped button of the sidebar, just under the shop (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.UtP5ShuRjXa3JrEZ.JournalEntryPage.mKZ6bak91UOPwDlM]{the sidebar}).

  2. Choose the Buyer at the top: their balance is shown.

  3. In the Models column (①), vehicles and drones are on two shelves, sorted by category then by name, with their attributes; click one. The Search field filters the list. You can also drag a vehicle from a compendium.

  4. In the centre (②), the vehicle's image between its gauges, then the equipment delivered with it. In the Modifications column (③), click a modification to add it: it appears in the centre with its category, its slots and its price on this vehicle; the bin removes it, Take the modifications off removes them all.

  5. Read the price (④), then click the buy button (Buy for…).

The showroom shows the vehicle's attributes once its modifications are installed, the printed profile struck through next to them; a factory modification is already counted in that profile, a modification waiting to be installed changes nothing (Rigger 5.0 p. 155). A vehicle or drone without its own image shows its category's image (bike, car, medium drone…), here as at the Workshop. In the shop, vehicles and drones each have their shelf: Vehicles (and their modifications (Rigger 5.0 p. 151-171)) and Drones (and drone modifications (Rigger 5.0 p. 122-128)).

  • A gauge shows what is installed, then, hatched, what remains to be installed: "0 + 4 / 18" reads "nothing installed, 4 to install, 18 slots". Going over is flagged: the extra installation will be refused (Rigger 5.0 p. 152).

  • The price: vehicle, modifications, express if open, Total, Availability of the lot (the highest of its elements, with the strictest legality) and Balance after purchase, in red if it is not enough.

  • The Dealer Connection quality of the right category takes 10% off the vehicle's price, after the availability surcharge (Rigger 5.0 p. 33).

What happens after the purchase

The vehicle arrives in the buyer's inventory with its modifications aboard, to be installed: they are installed by the book from the deployed vehicle's Workshop (@UUID[.uoPEUL919825Gedn]{6.2}). If the lot has an availability and the table plays with delayed delivery (Core Rulebook p. 418), it leaves as a single order, at the longest delay of its elements, and arrives assembled when the GM delivers it (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.bqnSE0NCUfCmiCd8.JournalEntryPage.Ga0gO6SMY0vVY4nv]{delivery}). An order is cancelled as at the shop, and the refund is that of the debit.

For the GM

The Equip (free) box equips any actor without debit, delivered at once. The modifications you add are marked installed by default as long as there is room left (the line's key changes this choice): the vehicle arrives with them installed, even after a delayed delivery. In the sheet's orders block, the GM's link on an order is Deliver now: to cancel, use the cancel icon.

House Rules — Express delivery

The book does not provide for paying to be delivered faster. If the GM has ticked express delivery, the dealership adds the express line to the price of a lot that is waiting, computed on the vehicle's full price. Unticked by default.

Related settings

← @UUID[.YTo9Tb6Bw8fuLkyp]{What the system does, settings and references} · @UUID[.Kyp3B3PN2QJ1zfc3]{6.4 Chases} →

All

What it is for

The GM runs the chase in a separate window: the vehicles engaged, their Current Speed, the range between each pair, the terrain, and who is out of control. Each chase action is a button that prepares the driver's roll and carries over its result; the system applies what the end of a turn brings about. The player rolls their own vehicle's actions from the same window.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU}

← @UUID[.I5GXBTreZxunHsIW]{6.3 The dealership} · @UUID[.NhvKN0LO55zGhs9Q]{Running a chase (GM)} →

Step by step: starting a chase

  1. In the token controls (left column), click the Chase tool, then Start a chase.

  2. Select the vehicles' and drones' tokens on the scene, then click Add the selected tokens. Each new pair starts at Medium range; the first vehicle added is the one pursued (the Role can be changed).

  3. Give each vehicle its Current Speed. For passengers, select their tokens and click Take the selected tokens aboard on the right line; the manual driver is counted aboard without being taken aboard.

  4. For each pair, set the range, or move it one step with − and +. Beyond the farthest, the pursued has lost the other (Core Rulebook p. 204).

  5. During the turn, tick Controlled this turn for each driver who took the Control a Vehicle action (Core Rulebook p. 202); a vehicle on autopilot is controlled by its autopilot. Then End of Combat Turn (with an encounter running, the turn follows its rounds and this button disappears).

At the top of the window, the GM chooses the chase system with a click (core rulebook or Rigger 5.0 advanced rules): it is the same setting as in Shadowrun settings. Each terrain in the list carries an example (Open: deserted road, city at night…), and under the list the book's examples for the chosen terrain are shown (Core Rulebook p. 200, Rigger 5.0 p. 173). Pursued and pursuers each have their colour.

The window's log (a scrolling box, 200 lines) and a chat message say what happened at each end of turn. The player who owns an engaged vehicle, or who is aboard, sees the window open on its own and follows it live; only their own roll buttons are active. They can close it: it no longer reopens at each of the GM's moves, even after a reload.

Out of control

A vehicle that nobody controlled during the turn is out of control (Core Rulebook p. 202): everyone aboard suffers −2 dice, and the system sets the effect on each; it removes it as soon as the driver takes control again. On the second turn without control, the autopilot takes over, if there is one. A destroyed vehicle leaves the chase at the end of the turn. End the chase clears everything, penalties included.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.Kyp3B3PN2QJ1zfc3]{6.4 Chases}

← @UUID[.Kyp3B3PN2QJ1zfc3]{6.4 Chases} · @UUID[.6aVi3OOfXZ3nGHk2]{Chase actions} →

Under each vehicle, the Chase action line: choose the action, the vehicle targeted (Against) when it requires one, then Roll. The list only offers the actions of the ruleset in force and of the vehicle's type; an impossible action (wrong range, already attempted this turn, vehicle lost) is refused with its reason.

How it goes

  1. The roll window arrives with the sheet's vehicle test, its threshold already set (terrain, maneuver threshold, Speed difference…) and the right limit; everything stays editable.

  2. If the action is opposed, the card carries an "… opposes" button, seen by the owner of the vehicle targeted (and the GM). They roll the same test, without a threshold; only one opposition per card: the button disappears once the roll is made.

  3. The GM clicks Apply to the chase on the last card: the system carries over range, roles, control, Speed, Handling or terrain. A card applies only once.

  4. When the action requires one more test (following a stunt, avoiding a crash, staying at Extreme range…), the GM's card carries one button per vehicle concerned, for its owner.

Action (core rulebook)What the system does with it
Control a Vehicle (Core Rulebook p. 202)no roll: the vehicle is under control this turn, the out-of-control penalty falls
Catch Up / Break Away (Core Rulebook p. 204)threshold test (maneuver threshold, Medium (2) by default, + terrain); one range per net hit, at most the Acceleration
Cut Off (Core Rulebook p. 204)opposed test, at Short range; if the initiator wins, the target makes a follow-up test, otherwise it is out of control and the GM decides on the crash
Ram (Core Rulebook p. 204)opposed test, at Short range; the card gives the damage to both vehicles
Stunt (Core Rulebook p. 204)for the pursued only; failed, it is out of control; successful, each pursuer follows it or falls back one range

What costs an action

The action you roll counts its Complex Action, on the combatant who acts: the vehicle if it is in the combat, otherwise its driver (the usual case: the rigger has the initiative, not their car). Opposing and follow-up tests are free, like a defense: neither action nor initiative (Core Rulebook p. 204). The vehicle test that follows your own action (avoiding the crash after your failed stunt) is free too: it is part of the action paid for.

Damage

When an action inflicts some (Ram, Collision, a failed Like a Boss), the GM's card carries an Apply Damage button per vehicle hit, seen by its owner and the GM: it opens the vehicle's resistance (Body + Armor, AP −6) (Core Rulebook p. 203-204) and disappears once the resistance is rolled. For a crash, the GM clicks the button that sets the crash damage: a value is offered, editable; a new card then gives a button to the vehicle and to each of those aboard (Core Rulebook p. 201).

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.Kyp3B3PN2QJ1zfc3]{6.4 Chases}

← @UUID[.NhvKN0LO55zGhs9Q]{Running a chase (GM)} · @UUID[.QqTr1CPKVq1xJEre]{The Rigger 5.0 rules} →

With the Advanced driving rules (Rigger 5.0) setting, the window follows Rigger 5.0 (Rigger 5.0 p. 173-182): Contact range before Short (and Visual after Extreme if an aircraft is engaged), six terrains from Open (+0) to Impossible (+6), a Current Speed bounded by Acceleration, a type per vehicle (ground, watercraft, rotorcraft, jet; an aerial drone enters as an aircraft), and fifteen more actions.

  • Opposed tests with a threshold (Catch Up, Get on Their Six…): the system counts the net hits (the initiator's minus the target's), then those that exceed the threshold. Neither the French nor the English edition says how the two combine (Rigger 5.0 p. 175): it is the system's choice.

  • Stunts are done on their own or built into another action (the line's Stunt field, the level is added to the threshold) (Rigger 5.0 p. 180). On rolling, the window asks for the benefit sought. Failed, the GM's card carries a free "avoid the crash" test, at −level in dice, threshold = terrain; failed, the vehicle is out of control. The book gives neither the sign nor the threshold of this test: it is the system's choice. The autopilot does not do stunts.

  • The driver's Edge: Zen Driving and Hang On Baby (jumped-in rigger), Falling Leaf (falling aircraft), crazy stunt; the window asks for confirmation before debiting the point (Rigger 5.0 p. 174-180).

  • The qualities Stunt Driver (+2 dice to stunts) and Relentless Pursuer (+2 dice to the actions rolled) are added on their own (Rigger 5.0 p. 33).

← @UUID[.6aVi3OOfXZ3nGHk2]{Chase actions} · @UUID[.ls3LnmQMXWVK6Ud6]{What the system does, settings and references} →

pages.name: What the system does, settings and references

text.content:
What the system does on its own

  • It prepares each chase roll (threshold, limit), carries over its result and writes it in the log.

  • It sets and removes the out-of-control penalty, hands control back to the autopilot, removes destroyed vehicles.

  • It counts down the action on the combatant who acts, and leaves opposition and follow-up tests free.

What the GM does by hand

  • Sets the DV of a crash, and applies the damage of Clear the Way, given on the card.

  • Plays the effects given on the card without being applied: perception (Crazy Ivan, tailing), shots (Strafe, Rake), a stunt joined to an attack.

  • Keeps track of the seats and the passengers' actions, and reads the tokens' position themselves: the range is the one they keep.

Related settings

Setting (Rigging tab of Shadowrun settings)Default
Advanced driving rules (Rigger 5.0)unticked: core rulebook chases
Actions rule lock (rolling without an action left)according to the world's preset (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.yj32FTBiKvVIyGIf]{the locks})

References

All

What it is for

Rigger 5.0 gives the rigger electronic warfare actions (targeting a device for their drones, confusing the opposing autopilot, breaking a target lock, reducing noise) and the possibility to make several drones act as one, as a swarm (Rigger 5.0 p. 30-31).

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU}

← @UUID[.ls3LnmQMXWVK6Ud6]{What the system does, settings and references} · @UUID[.vdNkRr4hF2fWeKko]{Electronic warfare actions} →

With the Use Rigger 5 Matrix Actions setting (Rigging tab of Shadowrun settings, unticked by default), these actions are added to the Matrix actions of the rigger's sheet, and are also launched with a click on the drone targeted in the PAN crown (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.CKM0UvZC23LLnCgv.JournalEntryPage.lDEaMIJ23r49haVj]{the radial menu}), including on an opponent's autonomous drone.

ActionWhat the system does with it
Target Devicedefense lost; the card offers to target the device (+N): until the end of the turn, the rigger's slaved drones (and their PAN's smartlinked weapons) get N more dice against it
Confuse Pilotdefense lost; the card offers the drone's Pilot × 2 test, threshold half the net hits; the GM plays the rest
Break Target Lockdefense lost, the sensor lock that drone held drops by N
Suppress Noisesimple test; until the end of the turn, the rigger's noise reduction rises by the hits, also between the rigger and their drones

The console's noise reduction is added to these actions' pool. The same rigger who rolls Target Device or Suppress Noise again replaces its effect instead of stacking it.

← @UUID[.qnNWcUI0hRMbFhqD]{6.5 Electronic warfare, swarms} · @UUID[.OfCIohrhdBY7Vzxg]{Swarms} →

Step by step: forming a swarm

  1. Install the Swarm program (a Mégapack rigging program) on the rigger's console and load it.

  2. On each drone's sheet, tick Slaved Device and give the same Swarm no. (0: no swarm). A rigger can have several swarms, one per number.

  3. Place the tokens on the displayed scene: at least two drones are needed. Under the number, the sheet says "Swarm 1: 2 drones, +1 to dice and limit", or why the swarm is inactive.

Each drone of the swarm takes the swarm's values (Rigger 5.0 p. 31): the highest Pilot (or the console's Device Rating), the highest Sensor and autosofts, the lowest Handling, Speed and Acceleration. At each action rolled from a drone of the swarm, two boxes ticked in the roll window add number of drones − 1 to dice and to limit; they are not offered for a defense or a resistance. A drone destroyed, bricked, no longer slaved or whose token is removed leaves the swarm at once; a stored drone does not count.

Backlinks: @UUID[.kFGMwUwhIDEOP3x4]{MENU} > @UUID[.qnNWcUI0hRMbFhqD]{6.5 Electronic warfare, swarms}

← @UUID[.vdNkRr4hF2fWeKko]{Electronic warfare actions} · @UUID[.9UjV231aFv9WUIcd]{What the system does and references} →

pages.name: What the system does and references

text.content:
What the system does on its own

  • It applies electronic warfare effects until the end of the turn, then removes them.

  • It recomputes the swarm at each change (drone added, lost, stored), for everyone.

What the GM does by hand

  • Plays the driving of a confused autopilot.

  • Decides on a swarm's initiative (the encounter tracker is unchanged) and rolls the scatter of the other drones' explosive weapons: the system rolls only the chosen drone's shot.

  • Removes by hand the one-turn effect of a character outside the combat.

References
